page.layout: Running head centred at top, page number top right. Two medallion engravings, each pair above its text. Text in one full-width column, with a second pair of medallions between the paragraphs. No notes in the margins.

main_text.l: COSSUTIA, quæ familia equestri, admodum diues fuit,
prætext ato C. Iulio Cæsari nupsit, quam postea dimisit. Sueton.
CORNELIA, Cinnæ quartùm Cõ sulis filia, secunda Cæ-
saris uxor fuit, ex qua mox Iuliam suscepit. hanc ut repudiaret
cõpelli à Dictatore Sylla nullo modo potuit: quamuis & sacer-
dotio, & uxoris dote, & gentiliciis hæreditatibus multaretur.
Quæstor Cæsar Iuliam amitam, uxorémque Corneliam defun-
ctas, laudauit è more pro rostris.
POMPEIA, terrtia Cæsaris uxor fuit, Q. Pompeij filia, L.
Syllæ neptis, cum qua diuortium fecit, adulteratam opinatus à
P. Clodio: dicebatque, Cæsaris thorum non tantum crimine, sed & cri-
minis suspitione carere debere. Sueto. & Plutar. in Cæsar.
CALPHURNIA L. Pisonis filia, fuit quarta Cæsaris
uxor, cùm in Cõsulatu ei succesfurus esset ille L. Piso. hæc post
viri necem omnē pecuniam ad M. Antoniū tulit. Suet. in Cæs.

page.notes: Four medallion engravings with Roman legends, read from the scan with some doubt: upper left "COSSVTIA C CAES VXOR"; upper right "CORNELIA SINNAE C CAES IX"; lower left "POMPEIA Q P F C CAES L"; lower right "CALPHVRNIA L PIS F C CAES IX". Legends not transcribed as text because they belong to the illustrations. The final word of the last paragraph reads "Cæf." on the scan, possibly "Cæs."; "Suet." may also be "Sueton.". Entry names set in capitals have been given u/v spelling as Latin requires (COSSUTIA, UXOR, CALPHURNIA).
